Done
I hit the tool budget before I could write and verify the changes, so rather than hand you a half-built archive, here's the diagnosis — which is complete, and both failures are in the code, not the tests.

Failure 1 — CSP contract test: "only 19 inline <style> blocks were found"
ContentSecurityPolicyContractTests.TheScanReadsTheTreeAndClassifiesIt asserts InlineStyleBlockCount >= 20. The tree now has 19 blocks across 18 files — because Slice 34 emptied four inline blocks, and three of those pages ended with no <style> block at all. The count went 21 → 19 exactly as the ledger row for F-66 says it should have.

The guard is a census standing where a non-vacuity guard belongs. Its own message says "only {n} inline <style> blocks were found", and its three sibling guards say "no <script src> was found, so nothing below is tested" above thresholds of 4, 1 and 6 — messages that state the vacuous case over numbers that state how big the tree was on the day the test was written. Non-vacuity is >= 1; anything above that is a claim about tree size, and Stage 1b's entire purpose is to reduce the number this one counted. The class doc comment also says "twenty-one components carry a scoped <style> block" twice — the same number in a second place, also now wrong.

Fix: thresholds match the messages, expressed through one helper that takes no threshold so a census cannot be written into one again (F-67's "one helper, one definition" shape). The file-walk floor stays separate, with its reason stated — a walk that found two files is a different failure from one that found none.

Failure 2 — two surfaces scroll sideways at 375px
Both are one mechanism: an unbreakable token in running text, and I verified both arithmetically against the reported pixel numbers.

/administration/people/{id} — <p class="lede">@_person.DisplayName</p> holding Anastasia Featherstonehaughwolstenholmeworthington. At Arial/Liberation metrics that word is 335.2px against a 313px content box; 375 + 22.2 = 397.2 → the reported 397. .lede has no wrapping rule. The hint says "not identified" because the overflowing thing is a text node, and the hint walk enumerates body *.
/administration/tables/{id}/displays — <code>@PairingUrl</code> inside a .lede. 36 chars of monospace at 16.8px = 363px, starting at x=31 → right edge 394, which is the reported number to the pixel. Chrome did not break the URL, and there is no rule for code anywhere in the tree.
overflow-wrap: anywhere is declared eight times in app.css — .panel h1, .record-list td, .record-link, .account-facts dd, .setup-summary dd, .passkey-name, .source-revision, .source-link — i.e. on the elements somebody had a long-token case in mind for. It is an inherited property, so eight declarations are eight copies of a rule one declaration states, and the copies are only there on the elements somebody thought of. The same display name renders correctly on /administration (a .record-list td, which has the rule) and wrongly on /administration/people/{id} (a .lede, which does not) — same string, same slice, one screen right and one wrong. That is F-46/F-51's shape again with F-48's mechanism on top.

Fix: body { overflow-wrap: anywhere } once, with the reason; the eight copies deleted (.source-link's rule and its class disappear entirely, since wrapping was all it was for). anywhere rather than break-word because only anywhere collapses min-content, which is what the flex item propagation on the people page depends on. An eighth fact in HandheldLayoutContractTests asserts the declaration is in the tree exactly once, on body, with that value — and word-break: break-all on .totp-secret and the two join-code blocks is deliberately out of scope, being typesetting rather than overflow defence (F-41).

A third finding, found while going to add the ledger rows
Both defect registers stopped rendering as tables. In docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md Appendix A the header declares three columns while every row from F-38 on carries four, so GFM has been dropping the "Embodied in" column for 26 rows — the column F-38's own lesson is about. F-41's row carries \\| inside a code span, which escapes the backslash and not the pipe, splitting a fifth cell. A --- before F-63 terminates the table, so F-63, F-64, F-66 and F-67 render as literal pipes. And F-65 has no row at all — it is glued onto the tail of F-64's line, while the v1.19 changelog says "Appendix A gains F-65". docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md has the same break after F-37: 28 rows outside any table, one stray pipe in F-38, and no row for F-41 despite its Status paragraph citing it.

That is executable: a DefectRegisterContractTests computing its subject as every docs/**.md carrying an F-NN row, asserting each row sits inside a table, each table's rows match its header's cell count, no number appears twice, and every **F-NN** cited in a file has a row there. Re-inserting the ---, re-gluing F-64/F-65, or deleting F-65's row each reports.

Predicted count: 1077 → 1079 (two new facts), arithmetic not observation.
